questions.stem: A 57-year-old man was brought into the Emergency Department in a state of collapse. He was known to have end-stage liver disease. He had been bitten on the calf by a neighbor’s dog 5 days beforehand. He had not sought medical care immediately following the injury. On examination, he was profoundly unwell. His temperature was 35.2°C, blood pressure 72/42 mmHg, heart rate 142 beats/min, GCS 14/15. There were multiple purpuric lesions over his torso and limbs. The bite injury was scabbed but clean, with no pus or erythema. Investigations: Creatinine clearance 30 mL/min Lactate 4.6 mmol/L
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.explanation: Capnocytophaga canimorsus Capnocytophaga canimorsus, commonly found in canine oral flora, can cause bacteremia and fulminant sepsis in humans, particularly those with asplenia or underlying liver disease. All of the organisms may be involved in bite injury infections, whether human, dog, or cat bite.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 4 Q28

questions.question: [image-based question: Staphylococcus streak on blood agar plate shown with satelliting colonies] Name 3 genera of bacteria that show this satellitism characteristic.
questions.question_raw: [image-based question: Staph streak on BAP shown with satelliting colonies]

parts.text: Name 3 genera of bacteria that have this characteristic.

parts_raw.text: Name 3 genera of bacteria that have this characteristic.

questions.model_answer: (1) Haemophilus (V-factor/NAD dependent, satellites around Staphylococcus which supplies V factor from lysed erythrocytes). (2) Aggregatibacter (formerly Haemophilus/Actinobacillus spp., similar V-factor dependence). (3) Abiotrophia/Granulicatella (nutritionally variant streptococci).
questions.beyond_mandell: Abiotrophia/Granulicatella satellitism is established microbiology, not stated in this chapter.

questions.question: Name the most likely pathogen for each of the following scenarios.
questions.question_raw: Name the most likely pathogen for the following scenarios.

parts.text: An acute myeloid leukemia patient with a central venous catheter presents with sepsis and hemorrhagic bullous skin lesions; the aspirate is growing a gram-positive rod.
An asplenic patient with sepsis after a dog bite.
A necrotizing scalp infection after swimming.
A common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) patient with chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea.

parts_raw.text: AML patient with central venous catheter with sepsis and haemorrhagic bullous skin lesions. The aspirate is growing a GPR.
Asplenic patient with sepsis after dog bite.
CVID patient with chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea.

questions.model_answer: a) Clostridium septicum (non-traumatic gas gangrene/hemorrhagic bullae in neutropenic malignancy, associated with GI/colorectal lesions). b) Capnocytophaga canimorsus - splenectomy is a strong risk factor for this dog-bite/scratch pathogen. c) Aeromonas hydrophila (fresh-water exposure necrotizing soft-tissue infection). d) Giardia duodenalis (lamblia) - the classic cause of chronic diarrhea in CVID.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the dog-bite answer (Capnocytophaga canimorsus) is grounded in this chapter; Clostridium septicum, Aeromonas hydrophila, and Giardia are established associations from general Mandell/ID knowledge, not this asplenia chapter.

questions.question: What is the most likely organism in each of the following scenarios?
questions.question_raw: What is the most likely bug in the following scenarios?

parts.text: Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
Common variable immunodeficiency with bloating and diarrhea
Cancer patient with bullous skin lesions and a Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli

parts_raw.text: Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
CA patient with bullous skin lesions and Gram stain showing GPBs

questions.model_answer: a) Capnocytophaga canimorsus — a slender gram-negative rod with tapered ends inhabiting the canine oral cavity; classic cause of post-dog-bite sepsis, especially in asplenic, alcohol-abusing, or otherwise immunocompromised patients, and may progress to DIC and purpura fulminans. b) Aeromonas hydrophila — wound infection/cellulitis after fresh-water exposure (others to consider: Plesiomonas, Edwardsiella; salt water: Vibrio vulnificus, Shewanella; and Erysipelothrix from fish/animal handling). c) Giardia duodenalis (lamblia) — the classic cause of chronic bloating and diarrhea in common variable immunodeficiency. d) Clostridium septicum — atraumatic (spontaneous) myonecrosis with bullous skin lesions and gram-positive bacilli, strongly associated with underlying malignancy (colonic adenocarcinoma, hematologic malignancy/neutropenia).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only part (a) is covered in this chapter; (b) Aeromonas, (c) Giardia in CVID, and (d) Clostridium septicum/malignancy are established associations from their respective Mandell chapters, not the Capnocytophaga chapter.

cohort_answer.text: 1) Capnocytophaga canimorsus. 2) Aeromonas. Others: Burkholderia, Edwardsiella, Plesiomonas, Pseudomonas. Salt water: Vibrio, Shewanella, Erysipelothrix. 3) Giardia. 4) Clostridium septicum (w/o trauma), due to the malignancy

questions.question: Name two gram-negative bacteria that are seen in aerobic and anaerobic blood cultures and that grow on blood agar but not on MacConkey.

parts.text: Name two Gram negative bacteria that are seen in aerobic and anaerobic blood cultures and that grow on blood agar but not MacConkey.

parts_raw.text: Name two Gram negative bacteria that are seen in aerobic and anaerobic blood cultures and that grow on blood agar but not MacConkey

questions.model_answer: (1) Haemophilus influenzae. (2) Aggregatibacter aphrophilus. Both are fastidious HACEK-group gram-negative organisms requiring enriched (chocolate/blood) media and failing on MacConkey. (Brucella and Pasteurella are also acceptable non-lactose-fermenting fastidious GNB.)

questions.question: Give the diagnosis in each scenario.

parts.text: AML patient with a line, fever and hemorrhagic bullae.
Asplenic patient with fever and hypotension after a dog bite.

parts_raw.text: AML patient with line and fever and hemorrhagic bullae
Asplenic patient fever and hypotension after dog bite

questions.model_answer:
a) Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum (hemorrhagic bullous skin lesions in a neutropenic AML patient).
b) Aeromonas hydrophila wound infection (freshwater exposure).
c) Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis (fulminant sepsis after dog bite in an asplenic host).
d) Scenario not recalled — insufficient information to assign a diagnosis.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the ecthyma gangrenosum item is in the Pseudomonas chapter (p. 2696); Aeromonas (freshwater injury) and Capnocytophaga canimorsus (post-dog-bite asplenic sepsis) are per their respective Mandell chapters.

questions.question: Name the MOST likely infecting organism in each of the following scenarios.
questions.question_raw: Name the MOST likely infecting organism in the following scenarios:

parts.text: A patient on eculizumab with fever, nuchal rigidity and headache.
An immigrant person who is undergoing rituximab therapy.
Therapy for multiple myeloma who presents with cough, dyspnea and a right-lower-lobe infiltrate.
A splenectomized person who had a dog bite 2 hours ago with bullae surrounding the wound.

parts_raw.text: A patient on eculizumab with fever, nuchal rigidity and headache.
An immigrant person who is undergoing rituximab therapy
Therapy for multiple myeloma who presents with cough, dyspnea and a RLL infiltrate
A splenectomized person who had a dog bite 2 hours ago with bullae surrounding the wound

questions.model_answer: a) Neisseria meningitidis — terminal complement blockade by eculizumab confers a >300/100,000 risk of meningococcal disease. b) Mycobacterium tuberculosis (reactivation TB) — B-cell depletion plus latent infection in an immigrant from an endemic region. c) Streptococcus pneumoniae — humoral/antibody deficiency of myeloma predisposes to encapsulated pneumococcal pneumonia. d) Capnocytophaga canimorsus — fulminant sepsis after a dog bite in an asplenic host.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only part (a) is addressed by this chapter. Parts (b) TB reactivation on rituximab, (c) pneumococcus in myeloma, and (d) Capnocytophaga in asplenia rest on standard host-defect associations (Mandell chapters on immunocompromise/asplenia, IDSA), not this Neisseria chapter.
